guides.wedding-pdf-editor.title: Wedding PDFs: Merge, Split and Print Without Surprises
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.desc: Prepare wedding documents for print and sharing: page sizes, bleed, embedded fonts, compression and a preflight check before sending to a lab.
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.lead: Most wedding PDF problems are invisible on screen: missing fonts, mixed page sizes and images that were downsampled during export.
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.f1v: Match the lab's template exactly, in mm or inches
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.f2v: Embed all fonts or convert text to outlines
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.f3v: Add 3 mm or 1/8 inch if any artwork reaches the edge
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.f4v: sRGB for consumer labs; ask before converting to CMYK
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.s1: Decide the destination before you build the file. A PDF for a printer needs a fixed page size, bleed and embedded fonts; a PDF for guests to read on a phone only needs small file size and selectable text. Merge related documents into one ordered file, then check every page for consistent orientation and margins before exporting.
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.s2: The US uses inch-based sizes such as 5 × 7 and 8.5 × 11; Europe and most of Asia use A-series sizes such as A4 and A5. Sending an A4 design to a US lab — or letter to a European one — produces unexpected cropping. Some professional presses request PDF/X with CMYK and a specific colour profile, while consumer photo labs prefer sRGB JPEG or a simple PDF. Always read the lab's spec first.
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.s3: Do not flatten a PDF that guests need to fill in, and do not 'print to PDF' from a browser without checking margins and headers. Watch for a font that looks right on your machine but substitutes elsewhere. If the file contains personal details such as addresses or a guest list, remove metadata and consider a password before sharing publicly.
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.q1: Why did the printer crop my design?
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.a1: The page size or bleed did not match the lab's template. Export at their exact dimensions and keep content inside the safe margin.
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.a2: Yes for any print PDF. Embedding, or converting text to outlines, prevents substitution on the printer's system.
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.q3: How do I make a PDF smaller?
guides.wedding-pdf-editor.a3: Downsample images to the target resolution, remove unused pages and metadata, and use the PDF's built-in optimiser. Do this on a copy, not the master.
